result:
The proposed answer of 128 is most likely wrong, though I could not verify the exact minimum from first principles.

The argument does not establish the claim. It says the first obstruction appears at central quotient order 64 because a Bogomolov multiplier is nontrivial in one isoclinism family, but it never explains how a nontrivial Bogomolov multiplier would produce an isomorphism of conjugacy quandles. It also does not justify why no counterexample exists below order 128. Non-isoclinic counterexamples of this kind usually show up at much smaller orders, and I believe the known minimum is 32, not 128. I have not confirmed this against the literature, so treat that value as a best guess.

Since the proposed value of 128 rests on an unsupported argument and is probably not the true minimum, I reject it.

VERDICT: REJECT
